author: reek
body: A self tail recursive loop whose tail-call argument is a bit operation must terminate and answer. On RISC-V these hung: the frameless tail call lowered two of its three argument paths with the general emitter, which uses a0 and a1, and in a frameless function a0 and a1 ARE the parameters, so the loop lost its induction variable and spun forever. The cross harness recorded that as a test producing no output at all.

author: reek
body: Each loop below selects a different branch of the frameless two- argument tail call, chosen by whether each argument reads the OTHER parameter. loop-both takes the both-read path, which was always correct; loop-a0 and loop-none took the two paths that were not. The three-parameter loop is the control: over two parameters the frameless path is not taken at all, so it answered throughout.

author: reek
body: These pass on x86-64 whether or not the backend is right, so this file earns its place in the cross battery rather than the default one. Keep the arithmetic loops beside the bit ones: an immediate-eligible argument lowers by a different route and stayed correct, which is what made the bit operations the suspect.
